title: Does the MuJoCo feeding-arm result change when the lips have the ISO/TS 15066 face stiffness and the safe force comes from the standard?
lede: at the ISO/TS 15066 face stiffness (75 N/mm) the blocked-arm impact peak only doubles (7.56 N against 3.68 N at 0.10 m/s), and every camera-arm trial stays under the 65 N and 130 N face limits (worst peak 53 N), where the assumed 2 N limit had flagged most; contact damping is unsourced and swept (MuJoCo, simulation only)
summary: osrobot-mjfeed assumed an 800 N/m lip and a 2 N comfort limit. This project re-runs the same MuJoCo feeding trial with the ISO/TS 15066 face effective spring constant (75 N/mm, 75,000 N/m) and the standard's face force limits (65 and 130 N; secondary sources disagree on which is quasi-static, so both are used). A 94× stiffer lip raises the blocked-arm impact peak about 2× (3.68 to 7.56 N at 0.10 m/s, 7.35 to 15.21 N at 0.20 m/s) and leaves the steady push unchanged. For the camera arm against a 30 mm sway (200 seeds), the share fed with peak contact within 2 N falls from 0.45 to 0.32 at 0.10 m/s, but within 65 N and 130 N it is 1.00 in every row; the worst peak is 53.3 N. So the assumed 2 N, not the physics, drove the earlier unsafe reading. Contact damping has no sourced value and is swept (blocked-arm peak 12.7 to 49.3 N from 100 to 1000 N·s/m at 0.20 m/s). Limits: the standard's tables were read only from secondary excerpts, lips are kinematic and cannot yield, pressure limits were not applied, tip mass, gains and sway remain assumed, no human model. Simulation only, not a safety case.
